whatIs.title: What is MacPacker?
whatIs.body: MacPacker is a free, open-source archive manager for macOS. Unlike Archive Utility — the built-in macOS tool that unpacks everything at once into a new folder — MacPacker lets you open an archive and browse its contents like a Finder window, seeing folders, file names, and sizes without extracting anything. You can preview individual files with Quick Look, drill straight into nested archives (archives stored inside other archives), and drag out just the one file you need instead of unpacking gigabytes. And MacPacker is no longer read-only: you can create ZIP and 7z archives from scratch, add or delete files in an existing one and save, or compress files and folders straight from Finder. Whether you're a developer pulling a single file out of a build artifact or just want to peek inside a download before unpacking it, MacPacker turns a clumsy multi-step chore into one drag. It supports 43 formats — including ZIP, RAR, 7z, TAR, DMG, and ISO — runs natively on Apple Silicon (macOS 14.6 and later), and is released under the GPL-3.0 license.

items.a: Yes. MacPacker is completely free and open source under the GPL-3.0 license. There are no paid tiers, subscriptions, accounts, or in-app purchases — and no ads or tracking.

items.q: What file formats does MacPacker support?
items.a: MacPacker opens 43 archive and disk-image formats, including ZIP, RAR, 7z, TAR (and tar.gz, tar.xz, tar.bz2), DMG, ISO, CAB, and more. ZIP and 7z archives can also be created, edited (add or delete files), and re-saved.

items.q: Does MacPacker work on Apple Silicon?
items.a: Yes. MacPacker is a native Apple Silicon app built with Swift and SwiftUI, and runs on macOS 14.6 (Sonoma) and later on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

items.q: How is MacPacker different from the built-in macOS Archive Utility?
items.a: Archive Utility extracts an entire archive at once into a new folder. MacPacker lets you browse and preview an archive's contents first, open nested archives directly, and drag out only the files you need — without unpacking the whole thing.
Install it from the Mac App Store, with Homebrew (brew install --cask macpacker), or by downloading the .dmg or .zip directly from the site. Every option is free.

items.q: How is MacPacker different from The Unarchiver?
items.a: The Unarchiver is an extraction tool: double-click an archive and it unpacks everything into a folder. MacPacker is an archive browser — it opens the archive like a Finder window, so you can preview files with Quick Look, step into nested archives, and drag out only the files you need. If you often want one file out of a big archive rather than all of it, that's the difference.

items.q: How is MacPacker different from Keka?
items.a: Keka focuses on creating and extracting archives across many formats with strong compression options. MacPacker leads with looking inside archives before anything is extracted: browse contents, preview files, navigate nested archives, and pull out individual files — and it also creates and edits ZIP and 7z archives. Both are open source; Keka still covers more formats for compression.

Yes. MacPacker is fully open source under GPL-3.0, so anyone can audit the code on GitHub, and it's distributed through the Mac App Store, Homebrew, and signed, notarized builds. It collects no data — archives never leave your Mac.

Yes — ZIP and 7z. MacPacker creates new ZIP and 7z archives from scratch, optionally split into volumes and protected with a password, adds or deletes files in an existing one and saves it, and compresses files and folders straight from Finder. It started as a browser and extractor, and write support for more formats is being developed in the open on GitHub.

press.boilerShort: MacPacker is a free, open-source archive manager for macOS. It lets users browse and preview the contents of an archive without extracting it, open nested archives directly, and extract individual files rather than the whole archive. It can also create and edit ZIP and 7z archives.
press.boilerLong: MacPacker is a free, open-source archive manager for macOS, written in Swift and SwiftUI. It lets users browse and preview the contents of an archive without extracting it, open nested archives (archives stored inside other archives) directly, and extract individual files instead of the entire archive. ZIP and 7z archives can also be created from scratch, edited by adding or deleting files, and re-saved, and files can be compressed directly from Finder. MacPacker supports 43 formats, including ZIP, RAR, 7z, TAR, DMG, and ISO. It runs on macOS 14.6 and later and is released under the GPL-3.0 license.
press.feat1Desc: An archive's contents, including file names, sizes, and folder structure, can be viewed without extracting it.
press.feat2Desc: Archives stored inside other archives can be opened directly, without extracting the outer one first.
press.feat3Desc: Individual files or folders can be extracted instead of the entire archive.
press.feat4Desc: New ZIP and 7z archives can be created from scratch, split into volumes and protected with a password, and files can be added to or deleted from an existing archive and saved. Files and folders can also be compressed from Finder. Write support currently covers ZIP and 7z.
press.scopeTitle: What it is, and what it will become
scopeIs: Opens, browses, and previews archives across 43 formats
Extracts individual files instead of the whole archive
Creates and edits ZIP and 7z archives — add or delete files, then save (ZIP since 0.18, 7z since 1.1)
Compresses files and folders to ZIP or 7z straight from Finder
scopeFuture: Write support for more formats than ZIP and 7z
Richer editing — rename, reorder, and more
Growing into a full general-purpose archive manager
press.scopeNote: Write support — in-place ZIP editing in 0.15, ZIP creation in 0.18, 7z editing in 1.1 — is the foundation for general archive creation and management. More will follow, format by format.
